title: Mark Duffy named Southport manager after interim spell
summary: Mark Duffy has been appointed manager of National League North club Southport after serving as interim boss for three games.
content:
The 40-year-old’s interim spell brought four points. His appointment is his first permanent managerial role since 2024, when he was in charge of Warrington Rylands. Duffy had been Southport’s assistant manager to Neil Danns, but stood down from those duties earlier this month before taking the top job.

Duffy joined Sheffield United in 2016 from Birmingham City and remained at the club until 2020. He was part of the side that won promotion from League One in 2016/17 and later reached the Premier League in 2019. In League One, he recorded six goals and nine assists in 39 appearances. He added nine goals and 16 assists in 72 Championship appearances for the Blades.

After leaving Sheffield United, Duffy played for Fleetwood Town and Tranmere Town before moving into non-league football with Macclesfield Town. He began coaching there, first as assistant manager and then as manager, before a player-manager spell at Warrington Rylands. He retired in 2024, aged 38.

Duffy joined Danns at Southport after almost a year out of the game and spent 53 games as his assistant. Southport have taken nine points from 10 games and sit outside the National League North relegation zone on goal difference.
